title: Behavioural Calls: Rule Out the Body First
next: Chapter 40, Lesson 2: Suicide risk, specific conditions, and safe restraint

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already secure the scene, run the primary survey, check blood glucose, and give oral glucose, glucagon and naloxone. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Rule out medical causes first, with a deeper assessment
  2. Interview well and run a mental status exam (COASTMAP)
  3. Handle consent, capacity and involuntary transport as the book describes

Textbook: Chapter 40, PDF pages 3402–3432
slides.say: Welcome back to class. Today we start behavioural emergencies. As EMRs, you've been on these calls: you stay safe, do a primary survey, check the blood sugar, and give oral glucose, glucagon or naloxone when the picture fits. As a PCP, you're expected to think one level deeper, because strange behaviour is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Today we'll cover three things: how to rule out medical causes first, how to interview a disturbed patient and run a mental status exam, and consent, capacity, and transport against a patient's will, exactly as the textbook describes it.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来上课。今天开始讲行为急症。作为 EMR，这类出车你们都跑过：保证安全，做初步评估，测血糖，情况相符时给口服葡萄糖、胰高血糖素或纳洛酮。作为 PCP，要求你多想一层，因为行为怪异是症状，不是诊断。今天讲三件事：怎样先排除躯体病因；怎样与情绪紊乱的病人交谈并做精神状态检查；以及严格按教科书的说法，讲同意、决定能力和违背病人意愿的转运。

slides.title: Body first: look for medical causes
slides.body:
Behavioural emergency: behaviour that threatens the patient's or others' safety

Strange behaviour is a symptom, not a diagnosis

  • Low sugar, DKA, low oxygen
  • Head injury, stroke, seizure, brain tumour
  • Severe infection, thyroid or electrolyte problems
  • Alcohol, drugs, withdrawal, some prescription drugs
  • Heart, liver or kidney failure
slides.say: A behavioural emergency is behaviour that threatens the safety of the patient or other people, like a suicidal, homicidal, or psychotic patient. Here's the most important idea of the chapter: strange behaviour is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Many patients who look psychiatric actually have a physical problem disturbing the brain, which the book calls organic brain syndrome. Think of low blood sugar, ketoacidosis, low oxygen, head injury, stroke, seizure, severe infection, thyroid or electrolyte problems, organ failure, and alcohol or drugs, including withdrawal. These are the causes you can actually treat on scene. Miss one, and you've labelled a treatable emergency as mental illness.
slides.sayZh: 行为急症是指威胁到病人本人或他人安全的行为，比如想自杀、想杀人或处于精神病状态的病人。这是本章最重要的观念：行为怪异是症状，不是诊断。很多看起来像精神病的病人，其实是躯体问题扰乱了大脑，书里称为器质性脑综合征。想一想：低血糖、酮症酸中毒、缺氧、头部外伤、卒中、癫痫发作、严重感染、甲状腺或电解质问题、器官衰竭，以及酒精或药物，包括戒断。这些是你在现场真正能治疗的原因。漏掉一个，你就把能治的急症贴上了精神病的标签。

slides.title: Clues that point to a medical cause
slides.body:
FindingPoints to medicalFits psychiatric
Consciousnessdecreased or fluctuatingusually alert
Orientationdisorientedusually oriented
Hallucinationsseeing, feeling, smellinghearing voices
Memorygaps filled with made-up storiesoften intact

Delirium: fast onset, fluctuates, usually medical. Dementia: slow; memory and judgment.
slides.say: How do you tell medical from psychiatric? Your mental status findings give strong clues. A decreased or fluctuating level of consciousness points to a medical cause; a patient with psychosis is usually awake and alert. Disorientation is most common in organic brain problems. Hearing voices is the most common psychiatric hallucination, but seeing, feeling, or smelling things that aren't there suggests something medical, like alcohol withdrawal. Confabulation, making up stories to fill memory gaps, also points to the brain itself. And keep two words apart: delirium comes on fast and fluctuates, usually from a medical cause; dementia is slow and mainly affects memory and judgment.
slides.sayZh: 怎么区分躯体性和精神性？精神状态的发现能给出有力线索。意识水平下降或时好时坏，指向躯体病因；精神病病人通常清醒警觉。定向障碍最常见于器质性脑病。幻听是精神疾病中最常见的幻觉，但看到、摸到或闻到不存在的东西，提示躯体原因，比如酒精戒断。虚构，就是编故事填补记忆空白，也指向大脑本身的问题。还要分清两个词：谵妄起病快、时好时坏，多由躯体原因引起；痴呆进展慢，主要损害记忆和判断力。

slides.q: A 62-year-old man is sweaty, confused and swinging at his wife, who says he was fine at lunch. He says bugs are crawling on the wall. After scene safety, what matters most next?
options: Start a full mental status exam to describe his psychosis
Primary survey, then check his blood glucose and SpO₂ and look for medical causes
Call police to take him to hospital against his will
Get his psychiatric history and medication list first
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A sixty-two-year-old man is sweaty, confused, and swinging at his wife, who says he was fine at lunch. He says bugs are crawling on the wall. After scene safety, what matters most next? A, start a full mental status exam to describe his psychosis. B, do the primary survey, then check his blood glucose and oxygen saturation and look for medical causes. C, call police to take him to hospital against his will. D, get his psychiatric history and medication list first. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位六十二岁男性满身大汗、意识混乱，正挥拳打他的妻子；妻子说他中午还好好的。他说墙上有虫在爬。确认现场安全后，接下来最重要的是什么？A 先做完整的精神状态检查，描述他的精神病症状；B 做初步评估，然后测血糖和血氧，寻找躯体病因；C 叫警察违背他的意愿送医；D 先问精神病史和用药清单。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Sudden change, sweating, confusion, and seeing things are red flags for a medical cause, and low sugar or low oxygen can be found and treated quickly. A mental status exam helps, but not before you rule out what could kill him. Forced transport isn't the first step for a man who may simply be hypoglycemic. History and medications matter, but they come after the primary survey and the quick checks.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。突然改变、出汗、意识混乱、看到不存在的东西，都是躯体病因的红旗；低血糖或缺氧能很快查出并处理。精神状态检查有帮助，但不能排在排除致命原因之前。对一个可能只是低血糖的人，强制转运不是第一步。病史和用药很重要，但要放在初步评估和快速检查之后。

slides.title: The PCP's hunt for medical clues
slides.body:
CheckWhat it can reveal
Vitals, GCS, temperaturefever, rising pressure in the skull
BGL, SpO₂low sugar, low oxygen
Pupilspinpoint → opioids; unequal → brain injury
Head, breathtrauma; alcohol, ketones, poisons
Skin, limbsneedle tracks, tremor, self-harm scars, one-sided weakness

PCP only: the functional enquiry, 9 body systems, including CNS and endocrine.
slides.say: As a PCP, your exam on these calls is a deliberate hunt for a medical cause. Take full vital signs with a Glasgow Coma Scale score and a temperature, looking for fever or rising pressure inside the skull. Check the glucose and oxygen saturation. Pinpoint pupils suggest opioids; unequal pupils suggest a brain injury. Check the head for trauma, and smell the breath for alcohol, ketones, or poisons. Look at the skin and limbs for needle tracks, tremors, self-harm scars, and one-sided weakness. Then use your PCP-only functional enquiry, which covers nine body systems, including the nervous and endocrine systems.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，这类出车中的查体就是有目的地搜寻躯体病因。测全套生命体征，包括格拉斯哥昏迷评分和体温，看有没有发热或颅内压升高。测血糖和血氧饱和度。针尖样瞳孔提示阿片类，瞳孔不等大提示脑损伤。检查头部有无外伤，闻呼气有无酒精、酮味或毒物气味。看皮肤和四肢有无针眼、震颤、自残疤痕和单侧无力。然后做你 PCP 独有的系统问诊（functional enquiry），它覆盖九个系统，包括神经系统和内分泌系统。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: when it's really medical
slides.body:
BC Diabetic Emergencies (incl. decreased LOC, no known cause) and Suspected Narcotic Overdose protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Primary survey; O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Vitals with BGL; check for stroke
  • BGL < 4.0, airway OK → oral glucose
  • EMR: can't protect airway → glucagon
  • Opioid picture: ventilate, give naloxone

PCP adds

  • IV access
  • Confirmed low sugar: D10W 10–25 g
  • Glucagon only if no IV
  • Transport after the first dose
  • Still unconscious + apneic: IV naloxone
slides.say: BC has no protocol for behaviour itself, but two protocols cover the common medical mimics: Diabetic Emergencies, which includes any decreased level of consciousness with no known cause, and Suspected Narcotic Overdose. On the left is what you already do as an EMR: primary survey, oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, vital signs with a glucose, a stroke check, oral glucose or glucagon for a sugar below four point zero, and naloxone once breathing is supported. On the right is new: the PCP starts an IV, gives D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, for confirmed low sugar, keeps glucagon as backup, and can give naloxone IV if the patient stays unconscious and apneic.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有针对行为问题本身的流程，但有两个流程覆盖常见的躯体「伪装者」：糖尿病急症流程，包括任何原因不明的意识水平下降；以及疑似阿片类过量流程。左栏是你作为 EMR 本来就做的：初步评估，给氧使血氧维持在百分之九十四或以上，测生命体征和血糖，检查卒中体征，血糖低于四点零时给口服葡萄糖或胰高血糖素，保证通气后给纳洛酮。右栏是新的：PCP 开静脉通路，对确认的低血糖给 D10W 十到二十五克，胰高血糖素作为后备；病人持续昏迷且无呼吸时，可以静脉给纳洛酮。

slides.title: Scene safety and first contact
slides.body:
• Plan your exit before you go in
  • Anything can be a weapon: a lamp, a chair, a book
  • Unsure you can manage safely? Call for help
  • Doesn't want to be touched? Respect it, unless it's medically urgent
  • Say who you are and why you're there; repeat it calmly
  • ABCs first, then take your time
slides.say: Safety first. Before you go in, know your way out, and remember that almost anything can become a weapon: a lamp, a chair, even a book. If you're unsure you can manage safely, call for help early. A disturbed patient may not want to be touched; respect that unless there's a strong medical reason, like heavy bleeding from a cut wrist or a falling level of consciousness after an overdose. Say who you are and why you're there, and repeat it calmly if they're confused. Handle airway, breathing, and circulation first, then slow down. Rushing can convince the patient that something terrible is happening.
slides.sayZh: 安全第一。进去之前先想好退路，记住几乎任何东西都能当武器：台灯、椅子，甚至一本书。如果没把握能安全处理，尽早求援。情绪紊乱的病人可能不愿被触碰，你要尊重，除非有充分的医学理由，比如割腕大出血，或过量后意识下降。说明你是谁、来做什么；病人糊涂时要平静地反复说。先处理气道、呼吸、循环，然后放慢节奏。匆匆忙忙反而会让病人确信出了可怕的事。

slides.title: Consent, capacity, going against their will
slides.body:
• Competent, conscious adult: consent is needed
  • Judged incompetent and needs care: may go against their will
  • Thoughts of harming self or others: should go, even unwilling
  • Any involuntary transport or forcible restraint: police involved
  • Follow your service's protocol; consult medical control

PCP angle: low oxygen, low sugar or a head injury can remove capacity. Treat, then reassess.
slides.say: Now consent and capacity, exactly as the textbook puts it. A competent, conscious adult must consent to go to hospital. If they refuse, they may be taken against their will when they're judged incompetent and need hospital care. Patients with thoughts of harming themselves or others should also be taken, even unwillingly. In every involuntary transport or forcible restraint, police must be involved. Laws differ between regions, so follow your service's protocol to the letter and consult medical control. The PCP angle: hypoxia, low sugar, and head injury can all remove capacity. You can now treat some of these, so treat first, then reassess.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲同意与决定能力，完全按教科书的说法。有决定能力、意识清醒的成人，去医院需要本人同意。如果拒绝，当病人被判定没有决定能力且需要医院救治时，可以违背其意愿送医。有伤害自己或他人想法的病人，即使不愿意也应送医。凡是违背意愿的转运或强制约束，都必须有警察参与。各地法律不同，所以要严格按你所在机构的规程执行，并请示医疗指导。PCP 的角度是：缺氧、低血糖和头部外伤都会剥夺决定能力。你现在能处理其中一些原因，所以先治疗，再重新评估。

slides.q: A calm, oriented man with schizophrenia refuses transport. His BGL is 5.2 mmol/L and SpO₂ 98%. He says voices are telling him to hurt his neighbour. According to the book, what is correct?
options: He's oriented, so accept his refusal and leave
He should go to hospital, even against his will, with police involved
You and your partner should restrain him now, before police arrive
Give him a sedative so he'll agree to go
slides.say: Let's check your understanding. A calm, oriented man with schizophrenia refuses transport. His blood glucose is five point two and his saturation is ninety-eight percent. He tells you voices are telling him to hurt his neighbour. According to the book, what's correct? A, he's oriented, so accept his refusal and leave. B, he should go to hospital, even against his will, with police involved. C, you and your partner should restrain him now, before police arrive. D, give him a sedative so he'll agree to go. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检验一下理解。一位平静、定向力正常的精神分裂症男性拒绝转运。血糖五点二，血氧九十八。他告诉你有声音叫他去伤害邻居。按教科书的说法，哪项正确？A 他定向正常，接受拒绝然后离开；B 他应该被送医，即使违背其意愿，并由警察参与；C 你和搭档应在警察到场前立刻约束他；D 给他一点镇静药，让他同意去。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A patient with thoughts of harming others should be taken to hospital even against his will, and police must be involved in every involuntary transport. Being oriented doesn't cancel that risk, so A is wrong. C is unsafe: two people are far too few to restrain anyone safely, and forcible restraint needs police. D is wrong too: sedatives for chemical restraint, like benzodiazepines, are not in BC EMR or PCP scope.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。有伤害他人想法的病人，即使违背其意愿也应送医，而且所有违背意愿的转运都必须有警察参与。定向正常并不能抵消这种风险，所以 A 错。C 不安全：两个人远远不够安全约束一个人，强制约束也需要警察。D 也错：用于化学约束的镇静药，比如苯二氮卓类，不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。

slides.title: Interviewing: talk is the treatment
slides.body:
On this call, you are the diagnostic tool

  • Set ground rules: crying is fine; hurting anyone is not
  • Open-ended start; let them tell it their way
  • Allow silence; name the feeling you see
  • Don't argue with false beliefs; one calm fact, at most
  • Ask "how" and "what", not yes-or-no or leading questions
  • Teens, severe depression, confusion: give more structure
slides.say: On most calls, your monitor and stethoscope do the diagnosing. Here, you're the instrument. Even your own feelings are data: if a patient makes you feel angry or uneasy, that may hint at paranoia or psychosis. And talking is treatment. Set simple ground rules, start with an open-ended question, and let the patient tell the story their way. Don't rush to fill silences. Name the emotion you see, like 'you look really scared'. Don't argue with false beliefs; at most, offer one calm fact. Ask how and what questions, not yes-or-no. If a teenager, a severely depressed patient, or a confused patient freezes, give more structure.
slides.sayZh: 大多数出车靠监护仪和听诊器诊断；这里，你自己就是诊断工具。连你自己的感受都是数据：如果病人让你感到愤怒或不安，可能提示偏执或精神病。交谈本身就是治疗。先立几条简单的规矩，用开放式问题开头，让病人按自己的方式讲。别急着打破沉默。说出你看到的情绪，比如「你看起来真的很害怕」。不和错误信念争辩，最多平静地陈述一次事实。多问「怎么样」「是什么」，少问是非题。如果青少年、重度抑郁或意识混乱的病人卡住了，就给更多结构。

slides.title: The mental status exam: COASTMAP
slides.body:
LetterLook for
Consciousnessalert? attentive or easily distracted?
Orientationyear or month; where they are
Activitypacing, tremor, frozen, odd movements
Speechrate, volume, slurring, strange words
Thoughtmakes sense? delusions? racing ideas?
Memoryrecent, remote, immediate
Affect / moodsad, elated, labile, flat, inappropriate
Perceptionhallucinations; ask gently about voices
slides.say: The mental status exam, or MSE, is the core of your focused exam here, and the memory aid is COASTMAP. C, consciousness and attention. O, orientation to time and place. A, activity, like pacing, tremor, or sitting frozen. S, speech: how they talk, the rate, volume, and clarity. T, thought: does it make sense, any delusions or racing ideas? M, memory. A, affect and mood. P, perception, meaning hallucinations. You get almost all of it by watching and listening; only memory, orientation, and sometimes perception need direct questions. Use these terms in your report, because the hospital speaks the same language.
slides.sayZh: 精神状态检查（MSE）是这里重点查体的核心，口诀是 COASTMAP。C 是意识和注意力；O 是对时间和地点的定向；A 是活动，比如踱步、震颤或僵坐不动；S 是言语：怎么说，语速、音量、清晰度；T 是思维：讲得通吗？有没有妄想或念头飞转？M 是记忆；A 是情感与心境；P 是知觉，也就是幻觉。几乎所有项目靠看和听就能完成，只有记忆、定向，有时还有知觉需要直接提问。报告里用这些术语，因为医院用的是同一套语言。

slides.title: Principles for every behavioural call
slides.body:
• Calm and direct; interview alone, partner talks to family
  • Sit at a 45° angle; keep your exit clear
  • No judging; honest reassurance, not "everything's fine"
  • Give a clear plan, then offer small choices
  • Never leave them alone, not even in the bathroom
  • Bring all their medications to hospital
slides.say: These principles fit every behavioural call. Be calm and direct; your confidence tells the patient they can stay in control. Interview the patient alone while your partner talks with the family, unless someone clearly calms the patient. Sit at about a forty-five degree angle, out of their space, with your exit clear. Don't judge, and reassure honestly; 'everything will be fine' sounds like you don't understand. Give a clear plan, like 'I think you need the hospital', then offer small choices, such as walking or the stretcher. Never leave the patient alone, not even in the bathroom. And bring all their medications.
slides.sayZh: 这些原则适用于每一次行为急症出车。冷静、直接，你的自信会告诉病人他们能保持控制。单独问诊病人，让搭档去和家属谈，除非某人明显能让病人平静。与病人大约成四十五度角坐下，不侵入对方空间，保持出口畅通。不评判，诚实地安慰；「一切都会好的」听起来像你不理解。给出明确方案，比如「我认为你需要去医院」，然后让病人做小选择，比如走过去还是用担架。绝不让病人独处，连上厕所也不行。还要带上他所有的药。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• No "psych" label until BGL, SpO₂, head and toxins are checked
  • D10W only for a confirmed low; recheck BGL and mental status
  • Naloxone can bring withdrawal and agitation: ventilate first
  • Psych meds act on the nervous system: think interactions
  • Calm body, busy mind: watch for escape or self-harm en route
  • Restrained? Warn the ED before you arrive
slides.say: Here's what's new for you as a PCP. Don't settle on a psychiatric label until you've checked glucose, oxygen, the head, and possible toxins, and keep rechecking. D10W is for a confirmed low sugar, so measure first, then recheck glucose and mental status after each dose. Naloxone can trigger withdrawal and sudden agitation, so support breathing first and be ready for an angry, awake patient. Most psychiatric drugs act on the autonomic nervous system, so think about interactions with your drugs. A calm-looking patient may still act suddenly, especially near the hospital. And if restraint was needed, warn the emergency department ahead.
slides.sayZh: 这些是作为 PCP 新要注意的。在查过血糖、血氧、头部和可能的毒物之前，别急着下「精神问题」的结论，而且要持续复查。D10W 只用于确认的低血糖，所以先测再给，每次给药后复测血糖和精神状态。纳洛酮可能诱发戒断和突然躁动，所以先保证通气，并准备好面对一个清醒又愤怒的病人。多数精神科药物作用于自主神经系统，要想到它们与你随车药物的相互作用。看起来平静的病人仍可能突然行动，尤其快到医院时。如果用了约束，要提前通知急诊。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: D50W → BC: D10W only, 10–25 g IV (PCP)
  • Hypoglycemia (BC protocol): BGL < 4.0 mmol/L
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, every 3 min, or 4 mg IN
  • Head injury (TBI), PCP: systolic > 120, BGL 4.0–8.0
  • EMRs have no IV access
  • Benzodiazepines are not in BC EMR or PCP scope
slides.say: For the BC exam, a few differences from the book. The textbook mentions D50W, but in BC the only IV dextrose is D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, a PCP drug. The BC protocol treats a glucose below four point zero millimoles per litre as low. BC naloxone goes zero point four, zero point four, zero point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, every three minutes, or four milligrams intranasal, with ventilation first. If a head injury is behind the behaviour, the PCP aims for a systolic above one hundred twenty and a glucose of four to eight. EMRs have no IV access, and benzodiazepines are not in EMR or PCP scope.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试有几处与原书不同。教科书提到 D50W，但在 BC 唯一的静脉葡萄糖是 D10W，十到二十五克，属于 PCP 药物。BC 流程规定血糖低于四点零毫摩尔每升即按低血糖处理。BC 的纳洛酮是零点四、零点四、零点八、再二毫克，肌注或静注，每三分钟一次，或经鼻四毫克，并且先保证通气。如果行为异常背后是头部外伤，PCP 的目标是收缩压高于一百二十、血糖四到八。EMR 没有静脉通路权限，苯二氮卓类也不在 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Body first: glucose, oxygen, head and toxins before any psychiatric label
  2. Talk is treatment: open questions, no arguing, COASTMAP in your report
  3. Involuntary: incompetent + needs care, or a danger to self or others; with police

Next: suicide risk, specific conditions, and safe restraint
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: body first. Check the glucose, oxygen, head, and possible toxins before you accept a psychiatric explanation, and use your PCP tools to fix what you find. Two: talking is treatment. Use open questions, don't argue with false beliefs, and describe the patient with COASTMAP. Three: a patient may be taken against their will when judged incompetent and needing care, or when they may harm themselves or others, and police must always be involved. Next lesson: suicide risk, the main psychiatric conditions, and safe restraint. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，先查躯体：在接受精神方面的解释之前，先查血糖、血氧、头部和可能的毒物，并用你的 PCP 工具纠正发现的问题。二，交谈就是治疗：用开放式问题，不和错误信念争辩，用 COASTMAP 描述病人。三，只有当病人被判定没有决定能力且需要救治，或可能伤害自己或他人时，才可违背其意愿送医，而且必须有警察参与。下节课讲自杀风险、主要的精神疾病和安全约束。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
